title: finding(core,data-objectstack): the OBJECT-FORM filter dialects still lower an empty or non-string `icontains` comparand onto the wire — the shape `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` declares REFUSED
body:
Restart-when: npm view @objectstack/spec version reports a version GREATER than 17.4.0 AND objectui's pnpm-lock.yaml resolves that version — that is the cheap trigger a sweep can watch, and it is ⛔ NOT the licence: on a hit, re-run the installed-surface probe in the hold comment and start work only when `isRefusedTextComparand` is reachable from the INSTALLED `@objectstack/spec`.
Restart-touch: pnpm-lock.yaml

Upstream (⛔ no longer a `Blocked-by:` line, because the target is CLOSED and a satisfied one makes the unlock scan re-fire on a card that is on hold): objectstack-ai/objectstack#18113, closed `completed` 2026-09-16. What still gates this card is the CONSUMER INSTALL SURFACE, not that merge — see the hold comment.

Found by the `os-dev` seat while implementing objectui#9001. Out of that card's scope: triage fenced it to `convertFiltersToAST`, and these are two different functions on two different authoring surfaces. Grading and `domain:*` are the triage seat's. Not claimed.

## The class

`@objectstack/spec`'s `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` carries two REJECTION rows for the case-insensitive contains operator — an empty comparand and a non-string one — each with `code: 'INVALID_FILTER'` and `mustMention` naming the operator. `ValueDataSource` has refused both **in both dialects** since objectui#8748: its `$` arm and its AST arm (`['name', 'icontains', '']`) each call `refuseTextComparand`, deliberately, because "`find()` picks between the matchers on nothing more than whether `$filter` arrived as an array or an object, so a door on one side only is a result that changes with the SHAPE of the filter rather than with its meaning".

objectui#9001 puts that door on `convertFiltersToAST` — the `$`-dialect producer. **Two producer paths that emit the same node are left without one**, and neither is reached by that card's fix:

1. `viewFilterRuleToNode` (`packages/core/src/utils/filter-converter.ts`, reached through the exported `toFilterNode`) — the STORED VIEW rule vocabulary. `icontains` is a member of the spec's `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS`, and the function's tail is `[rule.field, operator, rule.value]` with the value unread except by objectui#8557's array-arity guard.
2. `objectFilterEntryToAST` (`packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts`, reached through `translateFilterArray` when the filter is in `[{ field, operator, value }, ...]` form) — its tail is `[String(field), op, entry.value]`, and `FILTER_OPERATOR_ALIASES` carries `icontains` as an identity row. Note the object branch of `translateFilterToAST` delegates to `convertFiltersToAST` and therefore DOES inherit objectui#9001's refusal; it is only the ARRAY branch that does not.

## Measured

Worktree at `origin/main` `152f0a700` plus the objectui#9001 branch (so the `$` dialect is already closed), spec `17.4.0`:

```
toFilterNode([{ field: 'name', operator: 'icontains', value: '' }])    => [["name","icontains",""]]
toFilterNode([{ field: 'name', operator: 'icontains', value: 42 }])    => [["name","icontains",42]]
toFilterNode([{ field: 'name', operator: 'icontains', value: 'acme' }]) => [["name","icontains","acme"]]
convertFiltersToAST({ name: { $icontains: '' } })                      => THROWS FilterOperatorError INVALID_FILTER / 400
```

`objectFilterEntryToAST` was read rather than driven (it is not exported); its body is three lines and takes `entry.value` verbatim after `normalizeFilterOperator`, which answers `icontains` for `icontains`.

So after objectui#9001 the SAME wire node is refused when the author writes it as `{ name: { $icontains: '' } }` and sent when the same author saves it as a view rule or hands it to the ObjectStack data source in entry form. That is the acceptance-set split objectui#8447, objectui#8568, objectui#8976 and objectui#9001 have each closed on a different axis, restated on the DIALECT axis one layer up.

## Why this is a card rather than a same-PR repair

Three things the objectui#9001 fix does not settle, and the reason it was fenced away from them.

1. **Blast radius is different in kind.** `convertFiltersToAST` refuses a filter an author is composing right now. `viewFilterRuleToNode` refuses a rule someone saved months ago, and a throw there means the saved view fails at RENDER. objectui#8557's docblock argues that trade at length for the array case and concludes loud-beats-silently-empty; whether the same answer holds for an empty text comparand — where the pre-fix behaviour is "every row" rather than "no rows" — is the same weighing done again with a different input, not a mechanical copy.
2. **The message cannot be ported unchanged.** The `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` rows require the refusal to mention the `$`-dialect spelling. A stored view rule spells the operator without the `$`, so a verbatim port would prescribe a spelling the view vocabulary does not have. `ValueDataSource` solved this by naming whichever spelling arrived; a producer refusal has to decide what it tells a view author.
3. **It crosses a package.** The `data-objectstack` half is a second published package with its own refusal envelope (`MalformedFilterError`), so it is a second changeset and a second review surface.

## Not created by objectui#9001

Stated precisely, because the timing invites the wrong reading. Both paths lowered this node before that card and lower it after; what the card changed is that the `$` dialect no longer does, which is what makes the split visible. objectui#9001's own body already recorded the `data-objectstack` entrance as pre-existing — this card is where that observation gets a home, plus the `viewFilterRuleToNode` sibling it did not name.

## Dedup

Two channels, and the first one failed its own control — recorded because the failure is the documented one.

- **MCP `search_issues`**, repo-scoped: a first query returned exactly one result (objectui#8557) and did NOT return objectui#9001, whose title is near-verbatim for it; a second, shorter query (`icontains comparand guard`) returned `total_count: 0` for a subject that demonstrably exists. Neither is a usable reading.
- **Bounded REST listing**, `state=open` with `labels=bug,domain:ui`: 64 issues, one page, complete. Lit control: objectui#9001 is in the listing. Keyword sweep over titles and bodies for `icontains|comparand|filter-converter|FILTER_TEXT` returns three — objectui#9001 (this card's parent), objectui#9030 (the same function's TRUE-identity tail counting keys the loop skips) and objectui#9020 (a null-valued filter key getting two different row sets). None names the object-form dialects' text comparand. The nearest CLOSED neighbour is objectui#8557, which is `viewFilterRuleToNode`'s ARRAY arity on scalar operators — the same function, a different comparand question.

Refs: objectui#9001, objectui#8748, objectui#8557, objectui#8447.

Filed by an agent seat while implementing objectui#9001; the session reference for that run is `https://claude.ai/code/session_01MPaVWWMuWeT5LgB1qoXjVB`.
